newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Rupiah up on tighter liquidity.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Rupiah up on tighter liquidity.

text.p: * Indonesian rupiah rises on tightened liquidity, unloading of long dollar positions built before weekend.
* Malaysian ringgit trapped in tight range, upside limited by corporate dollar demand.
* Singapore dollar firms on fund sales of U.S. dollar but gains seen capped around 1.4440/45.
* Thai baht thinly traded with Thai markets closed for Coronation Day holiday and sluggish dollar/majors due to Tokyo holiday.
The Indonesian rupiah rose amid tightened liquidity on Monday as players unloaded long dollar positions built before the weekend.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,427.40/27.90 at 0420 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,429.0/30.0.
"Some speculators were unloading long dollar positions this morning," a Japanese bank dealer in Singapore said. But he said the dollar would be supported around 2,423.0/2,425.0.
Dealers said overnight money rose to a high of 15.0/16.0 percent before settling later at 13.0/14.0 percent.
A local bank dealer in Jakarta said rupiah buying by state banks on Friday and the central bank's neutral money market operation on Monday could have sparked fears of a liquidity squeeze.
Another dealer said there was limited room for the rupiah to strengthen as many operators remained concerned about possible violence during the election campaign ahead of polling day on May 29.
In Malaysia, the ringgit was stuck in a tight band due to a lack of fresh domestic leads and slow moves in the dollar/majors with Tokyo and London on holiday.
"It will be a very dull session today with movements likely to be limited to a 20-30 point range," a dealer at a Malaysian bank said.
Dealers said corporate demand for the dollar could again exert some pressure on the ringgit later in the day.
The ringgit was at 2.5079/89 to the dollar at 0420 GMT against 2.5080/90 at close of Kuala Lumpur trade on Friday.

The Singapore dollar firmed from its opening levels on European fund sales of the U.S. dollar. But dealers said its gains were capped as players were looking to buy the U.S. dollar on dips to around 1.4440/45.
A Japanese bank dealer said dollar/Sing showed potential to climb above a recent barrier of 1.4475/80 if the U.S. unit broke conclusively above 127 yen.
-- Syed Azman in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662-652-0642) and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
